Q: Errors when making tables with the flextable package A:

Your Header object is a matrix:

class(Header)
[1] "matrix"

You can convert it to a data.frame using as.data.frame()

library(flextable)
flextable(as.data.frame(Header))

Alternatively, you could use tableHTML which also accepts matrices:

library(tableHTML)
Header %>% 
  tableHTML(rownames = FALSE,
            theme = "scientific")

Q: How can I fix this javascript bug from Listal.com? A:

I have done the following:

  • Used the dev console and Tampermonkey userscripts to test POST messages, examine request and response headers from XHR network logs, verify various levels of variables, inject alternative requests, intercept and examine existing requests, go over all existing javascript for errors, compare using different cookies, and several more things I've forgotten
  • Used Puppeteer to attempt a more direct script injection, along with any number of attempts to log the results and understand what is happening.

The conclusion I have reached is the site expects a very specific response that cannot be locally generated (the AI called it "ephemeral", unknown if that's just AI or real). I do not believe this can be solved without involvement of the (absent) site owner.

For others who may stumble across this, and wish to attempt something similar on another website, here are some tools and suggestions:

  • The development console is incredibly useful. Most considering a project like this already have experience with it, but if you don't, F12 will bring it up in either Firefox or Chrome. For the uninitiated, it is a lot, but there are guides that help. In particular, when examining ajax calls similar to this, you'll be looking at the console for errors/warnings and to run local code for logs and checking things, and the Network tab to look at XHR entries (such as POST) to see the request and response headers, along with the actual response (if any)
  • Tampermonkey was very useful for generating scripts that can be set to "always on", which means you can leave a userscript going and reload the page without needing to remember to run the script repeatedly
  • Be sure to disable all browser extensions you don't need for your testing
  • Puppeteer was very useful for testing things Tampermonkey cannot. It is not, however, easy to use (for those unfamiliar with it, at least). You will need to have node.js installed, and then (in Windows) run the Puppeteer installer from a Command Prompt (or Powershell). It uses Chrome by default but can be made to use Firefox if you prefer.
  • Don't use notepad or wordpad or any other "default" text editor. Use dedicated coding software, like Visual Studio, or Notepad++, or something equivalent
  • Some responses will require a logged-in user. Depending on the site you are working with, don't forget that

Q: Setting postToAts in Interactive Brokers Python API A:

Steve D at Interactive Brokers support came through with the answer. I needed to set the contract exchange to IBKRATS, not just the order exchange.

Having fixed that, I also had to set o.notHeld = True and remove the line o.minTradeQty = min_trade_qty
